title: Jamestown and the Powhatan
objective: After this level you can explain how Jamestown survived after 1607, how tobacco made it pay, and how it collided with the Powhatan chiefdom.
summary: Jamestown (1607) nearly died in the Starving Time. John Rolfe's tobacco made it pay from 1614, but its hunger for land led to war with the Powhatan chiefdom in 1622.

cards.headline: England’s first lasting colony nearly quit. A Caribbean plant saved it.
cards.body: Jamestown survived disease, starvation and a powerful neighbor. Then tobacco made it pay, and set it on a collision course with that neighbor.

cards.headline: A bad place to build
cards.body: On May 14, 1607, the Virginia Company of London founded Jamestown, the first permanent English settlement in North America. The marshy site proved unhealthy: bad river water, mosquitoes and short rations brought dysentery and fevers. Moving into a swamp is rarely a good first step.

cards.headline: The powerful neighbor
cards.body: The land already had a ruler. Powhatan, whose given name was Wahunsenacawh, was paramount chief of Tsenacomoco, in tidewater Virginia. He had united dozens of tribes, more than 150 towns paid him tribute, and he was the highest authority in the region when the English built their fort.

cards.headline: The Starving Time
cards.body: In the winter of 1609 to 1610, drought, a Powhatan siege and scarce supplies left only about 60 of some 500 colonists alive at Jamestown. In June 1610 the survivors boarded ships to go home, but an incoming fleet ordered them to turn back. Jamestown was rescued on its way out the door.

cards.headline: Tobacco makes it pay
cards.body: John Rolfe replaced Virginia’s harsh native tobacco with milder plants from the West Indies. After he shipped his first barrels to England in 1614, other colonists saw his lucrative results and copied him. The colony had found its cash crop. It went up in smoke, profitably.

cards.headline: Peace, then war
cards.body: In April 1614 Rolfe married Powhatan’s daughter Pocahontas, and the marriage brought peace. (John Smith’s famous claim that she saved his life is doubted: some think he misunderstood a ceremony, others that he invented it.) But tobacco led settlers to press further into Native land. In 1622 Powhatan warriors led by Opechancanough, Powhatan’s brother and successor, struck back, killing 347 of about 1,200 colonists.

mascot.line: A common mix-up: Pocahontas married John Rolfe, not John Smith.

cards.headline: Jamestown: explained
learned: The Starving Time left about 60 of 500 alive at the fort
Rolfe’s tobacco, first shipped in 1614, made it pay
Tobacco’s hunger for land led to war with the Powhatan in 1622

questions.prompt: After 1614, the crop that made Jamestown profitable was _____.

options.label: cotton
options.rationale: The crop that sold in England was tobacco.

options.label: sugarcane
options.rationale: Not in Virginia; it was tobacco.

questions.explanation: John Rolfe’s West Indies tobacco, first shipped in 1614, made the colony pay.

questions.prompt: Put these Jamestown events in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Jamestown was founded in 1607, the Starving Time came in the winter of 1609 to 1610, Rolfe married Pocahontas in 1614, and Powhatan warriors led by Opechancanough struck back in 1622.

questions.prompt: Spain had founded St. Augustine in 1565. What was Jamestown the first of, in 1607?

options.label: Permanent English settlements in North America
European cities in what is now the United States
Towns ever built on the Atlantic coast

questions.explanation: Founded on May 14, 1607, Jamestown was the first permanent English settlement in North America.
